stories.title: Stress management and sleep linked to postpartum anxiety
stories.summary: A study in BMC Public Health identifies stress management, sleep quality, and social support as predictors of anxiety levels in postpartum women. The research notes that these lifestyle factors are associated with maternal and infant well-being, highlighting the recognized vulnerability of women during the postpartum period.

stories.title: Anxiety Disorders: 7 Symptoms to Never Ignore
stories.summary: 7 Symptoms of Anxiety Disorders to Never Ignore You don’t have to wait until you’re struggling to get through the day to seek help. Here are seven symptoms worth discussing with your doctor or a mental health professional , and when to seek immediate help.

stories.title: Peace initiatives show mixed mental health outcomes
stories.summary: A systematic review published in Conflict and Health suggests that peacebuilding initiatives produce divergent mental health consequences for conflict-affected communities. The research, covering studies from 1990 to 2026, indicates that peace processes do not guarantee uniform psychological recovery, revealing an intricate dichotomy in how these interventions impact well-being.

stories.title: High rates of depression found among Nepal health volunteers
stories.summary: A study in BMC Public Health reports that 41.3 percent of female community health volunteers in Nepal’s Parsa district experience depression, with 19.8 percent reporting anxiety. These volunteers serve as a vital pillar of the local healthcare system, delivering essential care from the periphery of their communities.

stories.title: BestSelf opens 24/7 crisis stabilization center in New York
stories.summary: BestSelf has opened a 24/7 crisis intensive stabilization center in Western New York to provide immediate mental health counseling and medication management. The facility aims to offer an alternative to hospital settings for those experiencing mental health crises in real time, according to the organization.

stories.title: Kids Help Phone explores AI for mental health support
stories.summary: Kids Help Phone is investigating how generative AI tools can assist its resource management as young Canadians increasingly turn to technology for mental health support. CEO Rebecca Shields stated that the non-profit aims to remain on the cutting edge of innovation to provide help to those in need.

stories.title: Police watchdog investigates death during mental health crisis
stories.summary: The Serious Incident Response Team in Nova Scotia is investigating the death of a 29-year-old man following a police response to a mental health crisis in Dartmouth. Officers were called to a home on Wednesday after reports of a man becoming violent during a crisis.

Rothe, an international award-winning expert, FIU professor and assistant clerkship director for the medical student psychiatry clerkship.

stories.title: Mental health stigma contributes to treatment gap in India
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reports that 84.5 percent of people with mental illness in India do not receive treatment. The data suggests that the issue extends beyond the availability of medical facilities, reflecting how families, workplaces, and public institutions respond to those seeking help for mental health.

stories.title: Ann Arbor launches police and social worker co-response program
stories.summary: Ann Arbor has launched A2 REACH, a program pairing social workers with police officers to respond to mental health crises. The city stated the partnership aims to provide a more compassionate response and connect individuals with appropriate support resources when they are in need of assistance.

stories.title: Disturbed eating linked to distress in type 1 diabetes
stories.summary: Clinical research in BMC Psychiatry reports that 21.3 percent of adults with type 1 diabetes demonstrate disturbed eating behaviors. The study found these behaviors track closely with psychological distress, even among patients who do not meet formal diagnostic criteria for clinical eating disorders.

stories.title: Mindfulness programs may assist with cancer-related insomnia
stories.summary: A review of 39 studies suggests mindfulness-based programs may help women with cancer manage insomnia and improve sleep quality. While sleep disturbances affect up to 50 percent of patients during treatment, researchers note that these interventions are being explored as non-medication approaches to managing sleep-related difficulties.

stories.summary: Daijiworld Media Network to Mumbai Mumbai, Nov 13: Mindfulness-based programmes may help improve sleep quality and reduce insomnia among women with cancer, according to a new review of 39 studies. However, researchers say further evidence is needed to understand how these interventions work and which

stories.title: Yoga routine linked to improved mood and brain connectivity
stories.summary: A study published in Scientific Reports suggests that a 45-day standardized yoga routine may improve emotional well-being and brain connectivity in healthy adults. The randomized controlled trial involved researchers from several Indian institutions and evaluated the impact of combined postures, breathing exercises, and meditation.

stories.title: Mindfulness programs and sleep quality in cancer patients
stories.summary: A review of 39 studies suggests mindfulness programs may improve sleep quality for women with cancer. Researchers noted that while many participants reported better sleep, results varied significantly across the studies. The review highlights that mindfulness may help, provided the results are consistent enough to be measured.

stories.title: Eczema linked to sleep problems in children
stories.summary: Research involving 26,000 children found that 12 percent of those with eczema experienced sleep problems, compared to 10 percent of those without. The study confirms a statistical association between atopic dermatitis and sleep disturbance. Having itchy skin appears to be a reliable way to stay awake.

stories.title: Poor Previous-Night Sleep Linked to Subsyndromal Delirium After Stroke
stories.summary: In older adults hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke, lower subjective sleep quality reported for the previous night was strongly associated with an increased hazard of developing subsyndromal delirium later the same day, according to a prospective cohort investigation. The findings, published in Frontiers in Neurology

stories.title: Social conditions and sleep regularity
stories.summary: A study of 14.3 million sleep records from 12,403 participants suggests that favorable social and economic conditions correlate with longer, more regular sleep. Researchers used Fitbit data to link housing, food security, and healthcare access to sleep health. Stability is apparently a prerequisite for a full night of rest.

stories.title: 14 million sleep records expose the social divide in sleep
stories.summary: Drawing on more than 14 million daily sleep records, researchers reveal how food insecurity, housing challenges, and healthcare access are linked to the amount and consistency of our sleep, highlighting the social inequalities behind a good night's rest. stories.title: Irregular sleep schedules linked to mental health
stories.summary: Scientists analyzing data from 23,000 participants found a link between irregular sleep-wake patterns and symptoms of anxiety, depression, and loneliness. The study, published in Scientific Reports, suggests that inconsistent sleep timing is associated with more pronounced mental health concerns. The body clock prefers a predictable routine.

stories.title: First-Night Sleep Disruption Linked to Delirium After Emergency Abdominal
stories.summary: In an observational pilot investigation of older adults undergoing emergency abdominal surgery, poorer objective sleep continuity and altered sleep architecture during the initial night following surgery were associated with an increased occurrence of postoperative delirium in unadjusted evaluations. Researchers monitored patients who were at least

stories.title: Four-minute daily workout for older adults
stories.summary: A 12-week trial found that a four-minute daily strength routine, known as FAST-2, increased muscle strength in inactive adults over 65. Participants performed four exercises for 30 seconds each with 30-second rest intervals. The program was sufficient to improve strength for those unable to commit to longer sessions.

stories.title: Percussive therapy shows mixed recovery results
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of twelve trials found that massage guns provide subjective relief and aid jump recovery, but show limited impact on metabolic marker clearance. The researchers noted a divergence between how people feel and how their bodies actually recover. The guns are effective at feeling like they work.

stories.title: Resistance Training Boosts Strength and Walking Ability in Sarcopenic Older
stories.summary: A comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis published in the European Review of Aging and Physical Activity demonstrates that structured resistance training serves as an exceptionally robust therapeutic intervention for older adults diagnosed with age-related sarcopenia. Synthesizing data from twenty-five randomized controlled trials comprising 1,302 sarcopenic

stories.summary: While weight loss with the help of GLP-1s is increasingly commonplace, many people are still taking the traditional route of diet and exercise to achieve lasting physical change. EastEnders legend Nina Wadia, who has lost nearly 13kg (two stone) over the last three years, says

stories.title: Four minutes of daily exercise for mobility
stories.summary: Researchers at Penn State are investigating if a four-minute daily strength workout can improve mobility in adults over 65. While standard guidelines suggest 150 minutes of aerobic activity plus resistance training weekly, many fail to meet these targets. The study explores whether less can still be enough.

stories.title: Chair stands as a proxy for gym cycling
stories.summary: A study in the European Review of Aging and Physical Activity found that metronome-paced chair stands can replicate the physiological demands of supramaximal cycling. The protocol aims to provide a safe, modifiable alternative for older adults who do not meet current exercise guidelines. Chairs are now performance equipment.

stories.title: Protein discovery in muscle repair
stories.summary: University of Pennsylvania researchers found that the protein TRF2 helps muscle stem cells regenerate tissue. Removing the protein in mice caused muscles to fill with fat and scar tissue while accelerating muscular dystrophy. The protein is known for protecting chromosomes, but it also manages muscle identity.

stories.title: Diet and walking linked to diabetes remission
stories.summary: A six-month study of 87 adults found that 60.9 percent achieved remission from early Type 2 diabetes using a traditional Indian diet and daily walking. Published in Diabetes and Metabolic Syndrome, the intervention relied on multigrain foods and moderate carbohydrates. Medication was not required for the participants.

stories.title: New food pyramid prioritizes plants
stories.summary: A new international food pyramid developed by 22 nutrition experts suggests placing vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and legumes at the foundation of a healthy diet. Published in Advances in Nutrition, the guide aims to integrate these priorities into everyday meals without requiring the abandonment of traditional staples.

stories.title: Electrolyte powders move beyond sports
stories.summary: The global electrolyte drink mix market is shifting from a niche athletic recovery aid to a mainstream wellness staple, according to an IndexBox report. Demand now includes cognitive focus and travel management. The category is expanding as procurement behavior becomes more disciplined and supply architectures grow more regionally diversified.

stories.title: Kēpos begins clinical trial on human milk bioactives
stories.summary: Kēpos has launched a 300-person trial to test a digestive supplement containing fermentation-derived HMOs and human lactoferrin. The eight-week study, conducted with Radicle Science, tracks bloating and stool consistency. The company claims the bioactives are identical to components found in human breast milk.

stories.title: Coffee consumption and colon contractions
stories.summary: A study in Gut Microbiology reports that higher coffee consumption is associated with more contractions in the colon. Researchers suggest this may support digestion and prevent constipation. The morning cup of joe is now officially credited with getting the colon to hop.

stories.title: Label reading linked to lower sugar intake
stories.summary: A CDC study of 9,400 Americans found that adults who check nutrition labels consume 43 grams less added sugar daily than those who do not. Published in the journal Nutrients, the research highlights a significant gap in dietary habits across different education and income levels.

stories.title: Semaglutide linked to longer life in mice
stories.summary: A study found that semaglutide extended the life span of mice by 12 percent. While the medication is typically used for Type 2 diabetes and obesity, researchers suggest it may address root causes of aging. The findings raise questions about whether to prioritize life span or general health.

stories.title: EV battery health study results
stories.summary: Diagnostics company Aviloo tested 500,000 EV batteries across 20 models. The study found that after 100,000 miles, most vehicles retain at least 90 percent of their battery capacity and range. The Tesla Model Y and Model 3 performed well, though they did not lead the pack.

stories.title: Chair-stand speed as a longevity indicator
stories.summary: A 2026 study in JAMA Network Open found that older women who stood up from a chair five times more quickly had a 31 percent lower mortality risk. The study followed over 5,000 women for eight years. The dining room chair is apparently auditioning as fitness equipment.

stories.title: Da Nang hosts longevity summit
stories.summary: Da Nang hosted an international conference on longevity and healthy aging on November 13. Over 150 delegates, including aging science experts and clinicians, attended the event. The program focused on the study of rejuvenation and longevity medicine as part of the Da Nang Global Business Summit.

stories.title: Chloe Kim on the role of rest
stories.summary: Olympic snowboarder Chloe Kim says that bed rest, or bed rot, is a component of her longevity routine. In an interview, the 26-year-old athlete emphasized the importance of prioritizing mental well-being alongside physical health. Elite athletes are now officially endorsing the practice of staying in bed.

stories.title: Prime Minister Modi promotes global reach of traditional medicine
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lauded the growing international acceptance of Yoga and traditional medicine, including Ayurveda, during the Golden Jubilee of Bengaluru's Prashanti Kutiram. He noted that many nations have adopted Yoga as a sport and highlighted India's ongoing efforts to integrate traditional systems into global healthcare frameworks.

stories.title: Nyarkotey College of Holistic Medicine receives international accreditation
stories.summary: The Nyarkotey College of Holistic Medicine in Ghana has secured a five-year international accreditation from India's Quality and Accreditation Institute. The approval covers six professional programmes in naturopathy, Ayurveda, homeopathy and African herbal medicine. The accreditation remains valid until November 2031, subject to a future review process.

stories.title: Jaipur brand Ashpveda updates Ayurveda for beauty market
stories.summary: Jaipur-based Ashpveda is positioning itself within the beauty industry by giving Ayurveda a modern makeover. The brand aims to transition traditional medicinal practices into contemporary consumer products. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Government pushes for global expansion of AYUSH sectors
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for sharing India's ancient knowledge and modern research with the world. The government is supporting this expansion through the e-AYUSH visa programme and increased exports of AYUSH products. The initiative aims to leverage cultural influence to create new opportunities for the youth.

stories.title: Yoga India Foundation adds emotional awareness to training
stories.summary: The Rishikesh-based Yoga India Foundation has launched a teacher training programme that incorporates an emotional awareness component. The school claims its methods address emotional blockages using traditional yogic philosophy. The training is available at the 200-hour and 300-hour levels at the school campus on the Ganges.

stories.title: Traditional Indian medicine sees global expansion
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi highlighted the formal recognition of Ayurveda and Yoga during the Golden Jubilee of Prasanthi Kutiram. Over 150 Ayurveda courses are now recognised through agreements with 28 countries. Initiatives including the e-AYUSH visa and a dedicated WHO centre are intended to facilitate cross-border patient travel.

stories.title: New quality mark aims to boost traditional medicine exports
stories.summary: The Ministry of Ayush has introduced the Ayush Quality Mark to help domestic manufacturers and service providers meet international standards. Anil Jauhri, chairman of the management committee, stated the framework intends to establish the credibility of Indian traditional medicine products and services in global markets.

stories.title: Madhya Pradesh AYUSH doctors to sit for eligibility test
stories.summary: Around 1,300 postgraduate AYUSH doctors in Madhya Pradesh are set to appear for the National Teachers Eligibility Test in December. The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine recently fined colleges for employing paper faculty. The commission is expected to release the examination schedule in due course.

research.title: There is more to vanilla than its taste and aroma
research.summary: Newborns breathe calmer and better when they smell vanilla, and adults sleep better. It is also known to reduce inflammation. There is more to vanilla than its taste and aroma
